summary.headline: Blue Cloud guides FY27 revenue of Rs 3,000 crore on a confirmed order book of about Rs 1,100 crore; Q4 margin rose to 17% from 12%.
summary.overview: Management said FY26 top line landed in line with plan, and Q4 gross margin expansion (reported margin up from 12% to 17% quarter on quarter, per an analyst) was attributed to productised SaaS and subscription revenue after about two and a half years of R&D. Management reiterated the Rs 3,000 crore FY27 revenue guidance and about 30% growth thereafter, but the call gave no quarterly split and the gap between the confirmed order book and guidance was left to organic and inorganic pipeline. Working capital was a visible weak spot: receivables spiked at 31 March 2026 and the current ratio was estimated by an analyst at about 1, which management expects to ease from the next quarter. The AIS Anywhere business is being moved from customised delivery to a SaaS model, which management said may reduce near-term revenue volume.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 operating EBITDA margin (as cited by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: Q4 margin cited as up from about 12% in prior quarter per analyst; company did not restate

financial_highlights.value: Rs 3 crore per quarter (as cited by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited Rs 21 crore in the last quarter, which conflicts with the Rs 3 crore figure and was not reconciled on the call

financial_highlights.metric: AIS Anywhere revenue, first half FY26
financial_highlights.value: Rs 170 crore to Rs 180 crore plus
financial_highlights.change: Annualised by analyst to about Rs 340-350 crore; management said 'yes'

financial_highlights.value: Management expects at least 5-6 percentage points improvement over current level; does not expect 50%

segments.name: Cybersecurity
segments.commentary: About 46-47% of closing order book; contracts mostly around five years, with the latest running to 2030. Products cited are BluTOR (dark-web incident tracking) and BluHawk (VAPT).

segments.name: Enterprise applications (AccessGenie, Blu Ra SAGA)
segments.commentary: About 24-26% of closing order book. AccessGenie is in SaaS pay-as-you-go use by state police and private clients; management cited 87-92% detection and 90-96% accuracy at the high end, without independent verification.

segments.name: Healthcare (BluHealth, BioSter)
segments.commentary: About 14% plus of closing order book. BluHealth claims vitals generation in 60 seconds from face recognition; BioSter is a sterilisation product beyond OT grade. Sold both direct and through partners.

segments.name: IT consulting / telecom
segments.commentary: Remainder of order book is domestic IT consulting. Telecom (5G CNPN and private network) is a future capex-heavy area; no revenue figure given.

segments.name: AIS Anywhere
segments.commentary: Acquired business; about Rs 170-180 crore revenue in the first half of FY26 per management. Being moved to SaaS with source-code ownership, which management said may lower near-term volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 3,000 crore reaffirmed; management described it as aspirational, supported by the Rs 1,100 crore confirmed order book plus pipeline in negotiation and MOU stages.
Management indicated a run-rate of about Rs 200-250 crore per quarter already in place for Q1 FY27; the analyst's Rs 750 crore quarterly figure was not confirmed by management.
Revenue growth of around 30% a year projected for FY28 onwards.
FY27 capex minimum of Rs 150-200 crore, with upside tied to telecom CNPN rollouts and edge data centres.
Depreciation expected at about Rs 80-100 crore in FY27 per analyst, which management said would not cross that range, depending on hardware mix.
Sustainable EBITDA margin cited as 10-15%, while Q4 was described as stronger and the trend expected to continue.
First data centre phase targeted for Q1 2027; management expects revenue from it in H1 2027 and margins above 'one-time plus' (not clearly defined).
capex_capacity: Minimum FY27 capex of Rs 150-200 crore, with upside tied to CNPN/private network telecom hardware and edge data centres.
First data centre line targeted to be ready by Q1 2027, with the Geo Impex land acquisition as the first step; BSE in-principle approval received, with further process still pending.
Management said it is moving to a less-capex financing model for telecom projects to limit depreciation.
Company currently uses third-party cloud, at cost of 15-20% and in some cases up to 35% of the cost base, which management expects to fall once own data centre is live.
Depreciation method is straight-line, per management.
demand_pricing: Government vs private mix cited as about 80:20 (private enterprise 80%, CGIS government/industrial/services 20%); management said this would stay similar in FY27.
Order pipeline for FY27 expected to be 75-80% private and industrial, with AI-first cybersecurity and AI governance expected to make up 40-45% of revenue.
International opportunities cited in Ghana, Liberia, Senegal, Mauritius and ECOWAS; management said some are at advanced discussion stage but not yet closed.
Receivables spike at 31 March 2026 attributed by management to slower payments from US and other overseas clients amid geopolitical conditions; billing is moving to a pro-rata model.
R&D spend over the last two and a half years put at about 10-12% of costs; management said focus shifts to CI/CD and iterative improvements instead of new R&D.
Management expects headcount to stay flat with attrition below 2-3%, with some recruitment for government PPP orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the closing order book split by segment, and is there a steady-state margin of 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cybersecurity is 46-47%, enterprise applications 24-26%, healthcare about 14%, and the remainder IT consulting. Management said margin could improve further, citing productised SaaS revenue and repayment of infrastructure investment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 3,000 crore FY27 guidance still intact given a Rs 1,100 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 1,100 crore is the confirmed recurring base; the rest of the guidance depends on pipeline in negotiation or MOU stage. It described the target as aspirational.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 750 crore quarterly run rate be achieved and how confident is management about Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aspires to the run rate given the order book and pipeline. For Q1, it stated stable performance at about Rs 200-250 crore for existing orders, with new orders expected to add to this later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company bridge the gap between current quarterly revenue and the Rs 3,000 crore target, and is Global Impex part of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bridge is a mix of organic and inorganic growth. Global Impex's full-year revenue was not disclosed; management said the target would be disclosed after the acquisition, and cited its EV and renewable energy order book.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables and the current ratio weak, and when will they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed receivables to slower overseas payments and a shift to pro-rata billing, and said the effect should show next quarter. No current ratio figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is AIS Anywhere revenue set to fall, and how is the BluBio sciences SPV accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the move to SaaS is a model change rather than a decline, with the volume expected to rise over time as the code is reused. On BluBio, management said it is not part of consolidated revenue at present and the contribution is through the AI healthcare platform.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility: Rs 1,100 crore confirmed order book against Rs 3,000 crore FY27 guidance; the gap relies on pipeline, acquisitions and new data centre revenue.
Receivables spike at 31 March 2026 and current ratio around 1 (analyst estimate); management expects improvement next quarter, which should be checked in Q1 FY27 numbers.
Revenue quality of AIS Anywhere as it moves from customised delivery to SaaS, which management said may reduce near-term revenue.
Telecom and data centre capex (Rs 150-200 crore minimum) and funding structure; depreciation could rise above the Rs 80-100 crore range discussed on the call.
Many KPIs were given verbally (margins, accuracy, depreciation, revenue split) without audited or reconciled figures; the Rs 3 crore vs Rs 21 crore depreciation mismatch in the Q&A was not resolved.
Global Impex acquisition: BSE in-principle approval received, with shareholder and other processes pending; its revenue was not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, AI platforms and the Rs 3,000 crore target, but noticeably vague or deferred on hard numbers such as quarterly revenue, depreciation, Global Impex revenue and the receivables timing. Answers on AIS Anywhere and the BluBio structure were defensive, and several questions went unanswered or were redirected.

adds.what: First data centre line (own data centre, Geo Impex land acquisition as first step)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 3,000 crore (called aspirational) against a confirmed order book of about Rs 1,100 crore plus, with the gap left to pipeline and MOU-stage deals; the first data centre line is targeted for Q1 2027 and FY28+ growth of around 30% is projected.
